A 28-year-old woman was critically injured after being stabbed multiple times in the neck while jogging along a Brooklyn waterfront path Friday night, as police seek information about the attack.

A 28-year-old woman was critically injured after being stabbed multiple times in the neck while jogging along a Brooklyn waterfront path Friday night, New York City police confirmed to Fox News Digital.

The attack occurred around 8 p.m. near Shore Parkway and Bay 17th Street in Brooklyn's Bath Beach neighborhood, according to the New York Police Department.

Police said the woman was jogging eastbound along the Shore Parkway Greenway when she suffered multiple stab wounds to the neck.

Emergency medical personnel transported her to NYU Langone Hospital-Brooklyn in critical condition.

MAN DEAD, ANOTHER CRITICAL AFTER DOUBLE STABBING AT BROOKLYN PARK AS POLICE DETAIN PERSON OF INTEREST: NYPD

A 28-year-old woman was critically injured after being stabbed multiple times in the neck while jogging along the Shore Parkway Greenway in Brooklyn on Friday night, police said. (Google Maps)

An NYPD spokesperson confirmed to Fox News Digital on Saturday that the woman remained alive.

Police have not released her identity, and investigators have not identified a suspect, the spokesperson said.

The New York Post reported that the woman had been training for Sunday's New York City Marathon, citing police sources.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, New York Road Runners (NYRR), which organizes the marathon, expressed sympathy for the victim and her family.

GEORGIA JOGGER RUNS FOR HER LIFE AFTER STRANGER ALLEGEDLY TRIES TO MOW HER DOWN 3 TIMES

The NYPD is seeking information about an attack that left a woman critically injured while jogging along a Brooklyn waterfront path. (Fox News)

"We were sad to hear of this horrible attack—our hearts are with her family and the running community," the organization said.

NYRR also said its records show the woman had previously participated in its races but could not confirm whether she planned to run in Sunday's marathon.

It was not immediately clear what led up to the attack or whether the victim knew her attacker.

The attack occurred along a section of the waterfront path overlooking Gravesend Bay, with views of Staten Island and the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge, the Post reported.

Police are asking the public for help as the investigation continues.

New York Road Runners expressed sympathy for the woman critically injured while jogging in Brooklyn, saying their thoughts were with her family and the running community. (Reuters/Brendan Mcdermid)

Woman who claimed she was viciously burned, left to die by boyfriend made story up: prosecutors

After a camping trip in New Jersey's Pine Barrens, a woman claimed her boyfriend set her on fire and had him arrested, but new information told a different story that saw him set free and her arrested.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

The woman who claimed her boyfriend viciously burned and left her to die during a camping trip in the Pine Barrens of New Jersey made the story up, authorities said.

Chelsea M. Villano, 33, of Eatontown, NJ, now faces two counts of falsely incriminating another person, according to the Ocean County Prosecutor’s Office.

The bizarre case began Oct. 15, when Plumsted Township emergency responders raced to the Pine Barrens after receiving a 911 call reporting a woman had been burned and abandoned at a campsite.

They found Villano burned and suffering from smoke inhalation, according to Patch.com.

She was intubated and flown by helicopter to Temple University Burn Center in Philadelphia, where she was treated and released days later.

“Her injuries were more consistent with a blowback of fire,” Assistant Ocean County prosecutor Mara Brater said authorities were told, reported Patch.com.

“Had she actually been submerged or [had fire] blown in her face intentionally, her injuries would have been much more severe.”

Villano told detectives that her boyfriend, Justin D. Martin, 36, splashed her with alcohol, then “tried to kill her and put her in a fire,” while they were camping with another man before fleeing in a Chrysler 200, according to Ocean County Prosecutor Bradley D. Billhimer.

Martin was arrested on Oct. 16 and charged with attempted murder and aggravated arson.

Three days later, Brater appeared before a Superior Court judge and asked that Martin be released, saying, “It was learned today that there are recorded statements of the victim indicating that this defendant didn’t have anything to do with the assault on her.”

On Oct. 23, the charges against Martin were dismissed.

Villano was released from the Ocean County Jail on Oct. 28, the prosecutor’s office told The Post.

The Pine Barrens are infamous as a mob burial ground, inspiring the famous episode of The Sopranos with the same name, along with the mythical creature, the Jersey Devil.
